questions.q:
From the statements given below :

(A) The angular momentum of an electron in $n^{th}$ orbit is an integral multiple of $h$.

(B) Nuclear forces do not obey inverse square law.

(C) Nuclear forces are spin dependent.

(D) Nuclear forces are central and charge independent.

(E) Stability of nucleus is inversely proportional to the value of packing fraction.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
(A) Electron revolves around nucleus only in those orbits for which the angular momentum is an integral multiple of $\dfrac{h}{2\pi}$.

(B) Nuclear force does not follow the inverse square law.

(C) Nuclear forces are spin dependent but charge independent.

(D) Nuclear force is attractive in nature. It is a non central force, meaning it does not depend upon the distance between the particles but rather upon their orientation. Nuclear force is stronger if the spin is parallel; and weak if it is anti parallel.

(E) The negative value (less quantity) of packing fraction indicates that the isotope is stable. Positive value of packing fraction implies unstable (radioactive) nucleus. Also, the stability of the nucleus is inversely proportional to the value of the packing fraction.

The nuclear binding energy& is the minimum energy that is required to disassemble the nucleus of an atom into its constituent protons and neutrons. Also, the energy of the nucleus is negative with regard to the energy of the particles pulled apart to infinite distance, because energy must be utilised to split a nucleus into its individual protons and neutrons. It is proportional to the& surface area.

Hence, statements C and D are& most appropriate.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
$A$. Atoms of each element emit characteristics spectrum.
$B .$ According to Bohr's Postulate, an electron in a hydrogen atom~revolves in a certain stationary orbit.

$C .$ The density of nuclear matter depends on the size of the nucleus.
$D .$~A free neutron is stable but a free proton decay is possible.
$E .$ Radioactivity is an indication of the instability of nuclei. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$( A )$ True, an atom of each element emits a characteristic spectrum.

$( B )$ True, according to Bohr's postulates~$mvr = \dfrac{nh}{2\pi}$ and hence electron resides into orbits of specific radius called stationary orbits.

$( C )$~False, the density of the nucleus is constant.

$( D )$ False, A free neutron is unstable decays into proton and electron and antineutrino.

$( E )$ True unstable nucleus show radioactivity.

questions.q: Mass numbers of two nuclei are in the ratio of $4: 3$. Their nuclear densities will be in the ratio of
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Radius of nucleus $R = {R}_{0}A\dfrac{1}{3}$

Density of nucleus \left(ρ\right) = \dfrac{Massofnucleus}{volumeofnucleus}$

$ρ = \dfrac{m \times A}{\dfrac{4}{3}\piR^{3}}$ ~Where $m$: mass of proton or neutron and~$A$: mass number.

$⇒ ρ = \dfrac{m \times A}{\dfrac{4}{3}\pi{R}_{0} 3 A}$

$⇒ ρ ∝ A^{0}$

Hence, density of nucleus is independent of mass number.

Therefore, the~ratio is~$1: 1$.

$

questions.solution:
$\dfrac{1}{2}\left(4m\right)v^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}\left(180m\right)\left(\dfrac{4v}{180}\right)2 = 5 . 5MeV$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{2}4{mv}^{2}\left[1 + 45\left(\dfrac{4}{180}\right)2\right] = 5 . 5MeV$
$⇒ K . E{.}_{α} = \dfrac{5 . 5}{1 + 45 \cdot \left(\dfrac{4}{180}\right)2}MeV = 5 . 38MeV$

The energy released in the fusion of $2 \mathrm{~kg}$ of hydrogen deep in the sun is $E_H$ and the energy released in the fission of $2 \mathrm{~kg}$ of ${ }^{235} \mathrm{U}$ is $E_U$. The ratio $\frac{E_H}{E_U}$ is approximately:

In each fusion reaction, $4{ }_1^1 \mathrm{H}$ nucleus are used. So,

in opposite directions with the same speed.

By conservation of momentum
$\begin{aligned}& \mathrm{p}_{\mathrm{i}}=\mathrm{p}_{\mathrm{f}} \\
& \mathrm{O}=\mathrm{m}_1 \mathrm{u}_{1+} \mathrm{m}_2 \mathrm{u}_2 \& \frac{\mathrm{u}_1}{\mathrm{u}_2}=-\left[\frac{1}{2}\right] \text { as } \frac{\mathrm{m}_1}{\mathrm{~m}_2}=\frac{2}{1}
\end{aligned}$
move in opposite direction with speed ratio $1: 2$

options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both& A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The binding energy for stable nuclei is always a positive number, as the nucleus must gain energy for the nucleons to move apart from each other. Nucleons are attracted to each other by the strong nuclear force. Binding energy per nucleon is almost constant in the range of& $30 - 170$. This is because nuclear energy is a short range force. It operates in the femto metre region.

Hence, this option is the correct one.

questions.q: Assume that protons and neutrons have equal masses. Mass of a nucleon is $1 . 6 \times {10}^{- 27}kg$ and radius of nucleus is $1 . 5 \times {10}^{- 15}A\dfrac{1}{3}m$. The approximate ratio of the nuclear density and water density is $n \times {10}^{13}$. The value of $n$ is _____.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
As we know,& $\text{density of nuclei} = \dfrac{ mass of nuclei }{ volume of nuclei }$

$⇒ ρ = \dfrac{1 . 6 \times {10}^{- 27}A}{\dfrac{4}{3}\pi\left(1 . 5 \times {10}^{- 15}\right)3A}$

$= \dfrac{1 . 6 \times {10}^{- 27}}{14 . 14 \times {10}^{- 45}} = 0 . 113 \times {10}^{18}kgm^{- 3}$

We also know that, density of water is~${ρ}_{w} = {10}^{3}kgm^{- 3}$.

Hence,
$\dfrac{ρ}{ρw} = 11 . 31 \times {10}^{13}$.

Therefore,~$n \approx 11$

questions.q: In a nuclear fission process, a high mass nuclide $( A \approx 236 )$ with binding energy $7 . 6MeV /$Nucleon dissociated into two middle mass nuclides $( A \approx 118 )$, having binding energy of $8 . 6MeV /$Nucleon. The energy released in the process would be _______ $M$ eV.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the energy released in the given process can be written as

$Q = B{E}_{Product} - B{E}_{Reactant} . . . \left(1\right)$

From equation (1), it follows that

$\begin{cases}Q & = & 2 ( 118 ) ( 8 . 6 ) - 236 ( 7 . 6 ) MeV \\ & = & 236MeV\end{cases}$

questions.q:
Two lighter nuclei combine to form a comparatively heavier nucleus by the relation given below:

& $X 12 + X 12 = Y 24$

~The binding energies per nucleon $X 12$ and $Y 24$ are $1 . 1MeV$ and $7 . 6MeV$ respectively. The energy released in this process is_____ $M$ eV.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Energy released in the given process = Binding energy of product $-$ Binding energy of reactants.

$= 7 . 6 \times 4 - \left(1 . 1 \times 2\right) \times 2$

$= 30 . 4 - 4 . 4$

$= 26MeV$

questions.q: The radius of a nucleus of mass number $64$ is $4 . 8$ fermi. Then the mass number of another nucleus having radius of $4$ fermi is $\dfrac{1000}{x},$ where $x$ is _________.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Radius of a nucleus is given by, $R = {R}_{0}A^{1 / 3}$.

Therefore, $R^{3} ∝ A$

$⇒ \left(\dfrac{4 . 8}{4}\right)3 = \dfrac{64}{A}$

$⇒ \dfrac{64}{A} = ( 1 . 2{)}^{3}$

$⇒ \dfrac{64}{A} = 1 . 44 \times 1 . 2$

$⇒ A = \dfrac{64}{1 . 44 \times 1 . 2} = \dfrac{1000}{x}$

$⇒ x = \dfrac{144 \times 12}{64} = 27$
